text:
Marta V: quick design check — thinking through how we surface rule conflicts in the Routing Policies editor. idea: show a compact conflict badge on the lower-left of the rule card + a tooltip that explains who wins. also announce to screen readers via aria-live. first pass microcopy below. thoughts? Diego R: +1 on the badge. we need to be clear about precedence — i keep seeing users confused which rule actually fires. badge should be scannable, not noisy. Ash W: microcopy options: 1) 'Shadowed by higher-precedence rule' 2) 'Inactive — matched earlier rule' 3) 'Overridden by rule above' Which reads best to non-technical PMs? Kevin L: i prefer #2 for simplicity. shorter. also: consider an icon + color blind friendly pattern (striping) so the visual state isn't only color. Sara T: accessibility notes: aria-live="polite" for incremental changes, but if conflicts flicker during drag-reorder it will spam SRs. propose debouncing announcements (500ms) and only announce when a conflict state is stable for >600ms. Marta V: good call on debouncing. UX question: should the preview panel highlight the winning rule and dim the shadowed ones, or just surface a hover tooltip? pros/cons? Diego R: highlight winning rule in preview — that gives immediate mental model. but in the rules list keep the lightweight badge so users can scan. Ash W: about validation behavior: live validation (while typing) is helpful but noisy. suggest: validate on blur + on save, with an optional 'validate as you type' toggle in top-right developer mode. Kevin L: design nit for badge: small square 12px, left stripe pattern for contrast, tooltip copy: 'This rule won't run because a higher rule matches the same input.' shorter alt: 'Disabled by earlier match.' Sara T: sample SR-friendly announcement options: - 'Rule alpha: conflict detected. Earlier rule "beta" will match instead.' - 'Rule alpha is currently shadowed by rule beta.' Pick short, include the name of the winning rule if available. avoid punctuation overload. Marta V: copy proposals for inline validation toast when user tries to save conflicting set: A) 'One or more rules won’t execute because of ordering — review conflicts in the list.' B) 'Save blocked: re-order or edit rules that are shadowed.' C) 'Save succeeded, but X rules are shadowed. See list.' Which aligns with product expectations? Diego R: we need an enterprise behavior toggle: either block save (fail loud) or allow save and warn (non-blocking). default to warn with clear remediation steps. so C + link to conflict list is ideal. Ash W: small interaction detail: when a rule is dragged, the badge should follow reflow and update counts. avoid re-render jumps. consider using placeholder-height animation. Kevin L: i'll add the pattern + palette. palette suggestions: - Green = active (solid) - Amber = partial match/warning (dashed) - Gray = shadowed (striped) + 60% opacity Will ensure WCAG color contrast and also provide an icon fallback. Sara T: also propose live-region example we can hand to eng: ```
Rule X is shadowed by Rule Y
// debounce updates before writing text ``` Marta V: ux tasks from this thread: - refine microcopy + pick official strings (Marta + Diego) - handoff aria-live pattern (Sara) - add palette + pattern assets (Kevin) - prototype animation for drag + badge reposition (Ash) - default save behavior: non-blocking warn and a setting to block saves for Dedicated customers (Diego) Diego R: timeline: aim for a small PR with copy + aria snippet this week, palette next week. next sync on Tue sync slot. ux-bot: reminder set for #product on 1769600000 (Tue) 09:30 to review PRs. :calendar:
